3be5878670448dcc.text: 1. 4 Professional Instructions for Use Essential Prescribing Information Device Name: Intuitive Ion Endoluminal System and Instruments (IF 1000). • Rx only: Federal Law (USA) restricts this device to sale by or on the order of a physician (or • properly licensed practitioner). Indications for Use The Ion endoluminal system (Model IF 1000), referred to in this manual as “the system, ” assists the user in navigating a catheter and endoscopic tools in the pulmonary tract using endoscopic visualization of the tracheobronchial tree for diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. The Ion endoluminal system enables fiducial marker placement. It does not make a diagnosis and is not for pediatric use. The Plan Point Software uses patient CT scans to create a 3 D plan of the lung and navigation pathways for use with the Ion endoluminal system. The Flexision Biopsy Needle is used with the Ion endoluminal system to biopsy tissue from a target area in the lung.

22f753311d318ca8.text: 12 Introduction | Professional Instructions for Use Intended Use The Ion System Cart (referred to as the System Cart) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract. The Ion Controller (referred to as the Controller) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract. The Ion Fully Articulating Catheter (referred to as the Catheter) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system for navigating to the target region in the airways. It is intended to also provide a conduit for the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe, Flexision Biopsy Needles and delivering compatible off-the-shelf tools. The Flexision Biopsy Needle is intended to retrieve tissue from a target structure. The Ion Peripheral Vision Probe (referred to as the Vision Probe) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system to provide live airway view for catheter navigation. The Vision Probe Adapter is intended to be used to connect the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. The Vision Probe Bag is used for temporary storage of the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe during a procedure. The Catheter Guide is intended to be used with the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to provide support. The Sensor Connection Cleaner is used for cleaning the sensor connections on the carriage of the Ion System Cart and the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. The Swivel Connector is intended to be used to connect the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to an endotracheal tube. The Suction Adapter is intended to allow modulation of suction when suction tubing is connected to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. Intended Patient Population The Ion endoluminal system (Model IF

a411d9f501bc53f3.text: 1000) is intended for adult patients suitable for bronchoscopy. Patient general health and medical history must be adequately assessed along with potential benefits and risks prior to performing procedures with the Ion endoluminal system. These include but are not limited to risks associated with pulmonary disease, severe pulmonary hypertension, cardiovascular disease, bleeding disorders, thromboembolic disorders, anticoagulation therapy, anatomical constraints, inability to oxygenate and patient suitability for general anesthesia. Intended User Only physicians with adequate training and experience in bronchoscopic techniques and adequate healthcare facilities should perform procedures with the Ion endoluminal system. Training provided by Intuitive is limited to the use of the Ion endoluminal system and does not replace the necessary medical training and experience required to perform diagnostic and therapeutic bronchoscopy procedures.

c19f5d48fec27e56.text: Introduction | Serious Incident Reporting 13 Clinical Risks and Benefits Patients should talk to their physician to decide if the Ion endoluminal system is right for them. As with any bronchoscopic procedure under general anesthesia, serious complications may include bleeding, pneumothorax (collapsed lung), cardiac-related complications, respiratory failure, air embolism, or death. As with other medical procedures, there may be additional risks associated with the use of general anesthesia and/or endotracheal intubation which are not listed above; patients should consult a healthcare professional regarding these and other potential risks. The overall benefit of the Ion endoluminal system is to bronchoscopically access and biopsy pulmonary lesions, including nodules in the lung periphery. The potential clinical benefits include improved or similar diagnostic outcomes of the sample obtained with comparable or fewer complications to other non-surgical approaches. The clinical benefits depend on a number of factors, including but not limited to nodule characteristics, patient medical history and disease state, and physician experience.

a60b55f71267d7ab.text: 1. 6 General Warnings, Cautions, and Notes Warnings WARNING: Before using the Ion endoluminal system (the system), review and understand the content in this manual and all accompanying manuals and supplements. WARNING: To prevent patient harm, use only instruments, accessories, and third-party products that are approved by Intuitive. Non-approved devices are not guaranteed to be compatible with the system. WARNING: Confirm that the sterile packaging for all single-use devices is intact and sealed before use. Do not use contaminated single-use devices or reuse single-use devices, as this may result in patient infection or equipment damage. WARNING: To avoid risk of electric shock or equipment damage, do not step on, crush/ pinch, crimp, or otherwise stress cables and connectors. WARNING: Do not reuse or reprocess single-use devices (such as the Swivel Connector and Vision Probe Adapter) after being removed from package, even if unused, as this may result in patient infection or device damage. WARNING: To prevent impaired ventilation and patient injury, the procedure should be performed under general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation, Electrocardiography (ECG) monitoring, and ventilator alarms. WARNING: If the system, instruments and accessories, or any of their components cannot be manipulated in a precise and controlled manner, discontinue use and contact Intuitive to prevent patient harm. WARNING: To prevent patient injury, do not use excessive force during the insertion or extraction of the Vision Probe or bronchoscopic tools through the Catheter tool channel. WARNING: Use fluoroscopic visualization (fluoroscopy) when advancing tools past the tip of the Catheter. Failure to use fluoroscopy during biopsy may result in patient injury. WARNING: Advance the Catheter only under live visualization from the Vision Probe (Live View) to prevent procedural delay or patient injury. WARNING: Do not activate the scroll wheel while interacting with the Controller touchscreen, as this may result in pneumothorax. WARNING: In the event of a medical emergency, follow steps to obtain immediate access to the patient (emergency egress), to avoid delays in patient care. WARNING: Do not contaminate instruments or accessories before or during use, as contamination may result in patient infection. WARNING: Handle biopsy needles with care to prevent user injury. WARNING: Always inspect the biopsy needle for damage before and during use. A damaged needle can contain loose fragments that may cause toxic reaction if left in the patient. WARNING: Use caution during biopsy of targets within 5 mm of the visceral pleura or other critical structures. Biopsy near critical structures may result in patient injury.

85047b79f29d5812.text: 16 Introduction | General Warnings, Cautions, and Notes Note: Always route the system cables away from possible tripping and stepping situations. Note: Before connecting any fluoroscopy equipment having no patient applied parts (that is, nothing comes into direct contact with patient) with this system, use device labeling to confirm that they comply with the standards IEC 60601-1 and IEC 60601-1-3. Note: All reusable devices must be reprocessed before use. Note: Use only water-based or silicone-based lubricants for the Catheter. Other lubricants may be difficult to remove during reprocessing and reduce the effectiveness of disinfection. Note: Navigation View should be used as guidance only. Note: Drive with caution in small airways where the airway diameter is smaller than the outer diameter of the Catheter. Note: Do not apply large volume suction through the Catheter tool channel when Catheter tip is wedged in small airways. Endoscopic Procedure Precautions and Notes Only physicians having adequate training and experience with endoscopic techniques should perform endoscopic procedures with the Ion endoluminal system. Medical literature should be consulted regarding techniques, complications, and hazards before performing any endoscopic procedure. CAUTION: High energy radiated light may be transmitted from the Vision Probe tip. High temperatures may exist in front of the light emission window. Exercise caution when positioning the tip of the Vision Probe to minimize tissue exposure to heat emitted from the light. Note: Use of the Ion endoluminal system may be associated with increased procedure and anesthesia time. Accessory Equipment Interconnection WARNING: Leakage currents from other medical equipment applied parts may be additive. To ensure maximum safety for the patient, only devices having Type BF or Type CF applied parts should be used with the Ion endoluminal system.

aa1b19f4dff8b75c.text: 4. 2 Plan Point Software and Planning Laptop Plan Point Software generates a plan of the patient’s airways from an existing CT scan, and the Planning Laptop is a portable computer used with the Plan Point Software. The CT scan images are uploaded to the Plan Point Software and Planning Laptop and segmented by the software. After identifying the target, the user can add a path to the target. The patient plan is transferred from the Planning Laptop to the Controller and displayed on the System Cart monitors for navigational guidance during the procedure. 9044478cde4bfbe6.text: 26 System Overview | Device Description Ion System Cart The Ion System Cart (referred to as the System Cart) consists of the instrument arm (with carriage), setup joint, brakes, and monitors (top and bottom). The instrument arm (referred to as the arm) adjusts to move the Catheter through the airway. The monitors present navigational information such as live video (Live View) from the Vision Probe, Navigation View, and biopsy target information. Third-party video sources including bronchoscope, fluoroscope, and radial endobronchial ultrasound (R-EBUS) can also be displayed on the monitors. For further information on System Cart use, see

26da72f647bc716d.text: The Ion Fully Articulating Catheter (referred to as the Catheter) has an approximately 3.5 mm outer diameter (at the tip), and a 2 mm tool channel that allows for insertion of compatible tools. It is compatible with the Vision Probe, Flexision biopsy needles, and third-party tools. The fiber optic shape sensor in the Catheter provides the shape and position of the Catheter on the System Cart monitors. The Catheter has an articulating tip.

6fb84af730bf06fd.text: The Catheter consists of the housing, sensor, input discs, shaft, tool channel, and tip.

335c02e2f84e33b6.text: The Catheter is provided non-sterile and is a multi-use device. See the Ion Instruments Reprocessing Instructions for further information.

b9b0d129c4b40e04.text: 490118) prevents fluid from entering the Catheter housing during reprocessing.

ebf7647c42509263.text: The Catheter Reprocessing Cover is provided non-sterile and is a multi-use accessory. See the Ion Instruments Reprocessing Instructions for further information.

b6a816a5bb7baf6b.text: The Sensor Connection Cleaner is used to clean the sensor connections on the arm carriage and on the Catheter.

5e0d4b4d27e173d6.text: The Ion Peripheral Vision Probe (referred to as the Vision Probe) is an endoscope that is compatible with, and inserted into, the 2.0 mm Catheter tool channel. The Vision Probe provides direct visualization of the patient’s airways during navigation.

fe4504ca55dd4b64.text: The Vision Probe consists of the lens (tip), shaft, Vision Probe Adapter ( Figure 4.7 , installed separately), cable adapter, leak test port, connector, and cable.

The direction of view of the tip is zero degrees. The field of view is 120 degrees. The Vision Probe has no user-serviceable parts.

faddb60b415b2039.text: 32 System Overview | Device Description The Flexision Biopsy Needles (referred to as biopsy needles, or needles) are flexible needles compatible with the Catheter. Biopsy needles come in 19 G, 21 G, and 23 G sizes and are protected by a flexible retractable sheath, with a stylet for support during insertion. The needle and sheath tip are radiopaque for visualization under fluoroscopy. The needle handle contains a catch (detent) that creates resistance to hold the handle in place until the user pushes the handle past the catch (detent). The needle stop allows the user to control the needle length (up to 3 cm). The biopsy needles are packaged with a compatible three-way valve and vacuum syringe. The biopsy needles are single-use devices provided sterile by Ethylene Oxide (EO) sterilization method. For replacement, contact Customer Service.

d83e92fc6b24fe7a.text: 4. 3 Controller Use The Controller provides controls to insert, retract, and articulate the Catheter. Note: If friction is felt in the trackball or scroll wheel, clean it with saline and dry with gauze prior to or during use, as needed. Note: Calibration initiates after installing the trackball and scroll wheel. Do not touch the trackball or scroll wheel during calibration. Note: If Controller responsiveness is poor, change or dry gloves. The Controller touchscreen and scroll wheel are designed to sense touch. Wet gloves may interfere with touch sensing. Figure

38e6228941f99f64.text: 4. 19 Controller 4 3 5 6 2 1 7 8 10 9 The Controller has the following components:

1050760a3e10b997.text: 1. Handle: Provides grasp for transport of the Controller.

dd9f332b6495256d.text: 2. Emergency stop (E-stop) button: Stops system operation at any time and causes the Catheter tip to go inactive.

184b5f0b0d5b0690.text: 3. Scroll wheel: Controls the insertion and retraction of the Catheter. Roll it towards the touchscreen to insert the Catheter, and roll it away from the touchscreen to retract it.

b6a1dfb11279b551.text: 4. Passive button: Controls the Catheter state (active and passive). Quick-press this button to relax the Catheter tip (passive), and press it again to resume active mode. Press and hold to slowly relax the Catheter tip (temporary passive). Release the button to stop relaxing the Catheter and resume active mode.

8281109cd7b65699.text: 5. Touchscreen: Controls to select targets, save images and videos, and provide other options described in this manual.

caa7c16c3d74684b.text: 6. Trackball: Controls the articulation of the Catheter tip. Roll the trackball right to move the Catheter tip to the right, roll the trackball left to move the Catheter tip to the left. Roll up and down to move the Catheter tip up and down.

ac00625e2c059582.text: 9. 1 Register WARNING: To prevent impaired ventilation and patient injury, the procedure should be performed under general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation, Electrocardiography (ECG) monitoring, and ventilator alarms. Registration is the process used to match the airway Live View with the Navigation View. During registration, the system collects apical and basal data for each lung. These apical and basal segments are displayed on the system as four quadrants, which are regional divisions of the Airway Tree (that is, the quadrants are not anatomically divided by lobe). Follow the steps on the top monitor to perform airway registration.

5d2295ebcbfd5fdd.text: 1. Drive to main carina. a. Match the Live View to the Navigation View in centering, depth, and rotation. If the views do not match, adjust the Live View as needed. Adjust centering using the trackball, adjust depth using the scroll wheel, or adjust rotation using the Controller touchscreen. b. Tap Confirm Main Carina on the Controller touchscreen.

3804409feef48174.text: 2. If you would like to start video recording, tap Start Video. This button is always accessible from the Quick Tools panel.

d296546c11a6b5af.text: 3. Start survey by driving into each main bronchus until the right and left indicators are illuminated.

a1774a53bd920afa.text: 4. Drive into one apical and one basal segment in each lung until the indicator for each quadrant illuminates. The border of the quadrant you are currently in is highlighted. Note: Use Show Lung Regions to display the separation of the lung into the four quadrants with their associated colors on the Airway Tree (note that these quadrants are not based on lobes). If the system checks the wrong quadrant, continue to drive to all four apical and basal regions of the lung. If quadrant checks are missing after you have navigated to all four regions, proceed with partial registration. It is not recommended to continue navigating to get all four quadrant checks if apical and basal data has been gathered. Figure

23cc11cdb5a8a34c.text: 5. Evaluate registration and tap Accept Registration or Redo Registration on the Controller touchscreen. To evaluate registration, navigate beyond the main carina and evaluate the relationship between the Live View and the Navigation View, especially at carinas proximal to the region of interest. Some discrepancy may occur due to biological motion. Redo registration if there is a visual mismatch between the Live View and Navigation View • during navigation, or if there is significant patient or system movement. Redo registration if the Swivel Connector is undocked from the arm, the arm clutch button is • pressed, the System Cart brakes are unlocked, or the Catheter is removed from the system mid-procedure.

b0360f4aae13b917.text: 9. 2 Navigate After registration is complete, the first planned destination (target and path) automatically appears on screen. The planned pathway to the target appears on the Navigation View, Tree View, and Progress View. It is possible to switch to an alternate target or pathway if one was planned. Navigation of the Catheter through the airways should be performed in a minimally traumatic manner by attempting to stay in the center of the airways at all times. WARNING: Advance the Catheter only under live visualization from the Vision Probe (Live View) to prevent procedural delay or patient injury. WARNING: Do not activate the scroll wheel while interacting with the Controller touchscreen, as this may result in pneumothorax. Note: Navigation View should be used as guidance only. Note: The Swivel Connector may partially disconnect from the arm due to Catheter buckling or excessive friction in the ET tube. Ensure sufficient lubrication is applied to the Catheter. To navigate to the target and position the Catheter for biopsy:

3f0495fcc3dae7b1.text: 1. Use the Controller to drive the Catheter through the planned pathway to the target. Watch the Live View while driving.

4288e77b444ef1fb.text: 2. Once the target is reached, note the message to use fluoroscopic guidance when extending tools past the tip of the Catheter.

If the stripes are not visible, a message appears when the Vision Probe reaches the Catheter tip. The message indicates that orientation was not accurately detected and instructs you to partially retract the Vision Probe until the stripes inside the Catheter are clearly visible, and then reinsert the Vision Probe through the Catheter. Always make sure the Vision Probe tip is clean. If the system does not present the message because it did not detect the stripes (or if it detects the stripes incorrectly), the Vision Probe image will appear to be 90 or 180 degrees rotated, and driving will be non-intuitive. In this case, partially retract the Vision Probe until the stripes inside the Catheter are clearly visible, and then reinsert the Vision Probe through the Catheter. If the issue persists, try replacing the Vision Probe, the Catheter, or both. 447a044361cba201.text: System Specifications | Electromagnetic Compatibility 111 D. 7 Electromagnetic Compatibility The Ion System with On Site has been tested and found to be in compliance with IEC 60601-1-2, International standard for Medical electrical equipment - Part 1-2: General requirements for basic safety and essential performance - Collateral standard: Electromagnetic compatibility Requirements and tests. It is intended to be used in a procedure room environment and operation of the system is unaffected when used in the electromagnetic environment as specified in Tables 1– 3 in this section. Special precautions and installation information for the system for Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) are provided in this section, see EMC Tables on page 111. The performance of the system is unaffected when exposed to the electromagnetic environment as described in the IEC 60601-1-2 standard. There is no degradation of performance and therefore no risks to the patient or other devices due to Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) when used in the electromagnetic environment as specified in the tables in this section. WARNING: Use of this equipment adjacent to or stacked with other equipment should be avoided because it could result in improper operation. If such use is necessary, this equipment and the other equipment should be observed to verify that they are operating normally. WARNING: Use of accessories, transducers, and cables other than those specified or provided by the manufacturer of this equipment could result in increased electromagnetic emissions or decreased electromagnetic immunity of this equipment and result in improper operation. Note: The Ion system was tested with shielded 3-meter composite video, S-video, SDI, DVI, HDMI, and Ethernet cables. c26113557dc1b869.text: 122 Glossary Appendix G Glossary Table G. 1 Glossary Meaning Term 3 D Three-dimensional. AC Alternating current, also represented by the AC symbol: ~. “AC” or “AC power” refers to electrical connection to a wall outlet, as opposed to battery power. AP View Anterior-posterior view. Head on view of the airway tree looking straight at the patient’s chest. Arm The instrument arm on the System Cart that supports the Catheter, Catheter Guide, Vision Probe, and accessories. BF or Type BF An IEC 60601-1 classification for patient applied parts. A Type BF classification indicates an applied part that is not suitable for direct conductive contact with the heart or other applications as considered necessary. Bronchoscopy An endoscopic technique of visualizing the inside of the airways for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes where a bronchoscope is introduced through nose or mouth. It is a non-sterile procedure. Bronch Suite See Procedure Room. C-arm See fluoroscope. CF or Type CF An IEC 60601-1 classification for patient applied parts. Type CF is the most stringent classification, being required for those applications where the applied part is in direct conductive contact with the heart or other applications as considered necessary. CAUTION A caution alerts the reader about a potentially hazardous situation which, if not avoided, may result in minor or moderate injury to the user or patient or damage to the equipment or other property. It may also be used to alert against unsafe practices. This includes the special care necessary for the safe and effective use of the device and the care necessary to avoid damage to a device that may occur as a result of use or misuse. CSSD See SPD. Carriage The mechanism on the arm that supports the Catheter. Provides the insertion and retraction motion of the Catheter. Circulating nurse A circulating nurse is a non-sterile user. (continues on next page)

b91c0c34c92e7950.text: Glossary 123 Table G. 1 Glossary (continued) Meaning Term Clutch button Used to position the arm. There are two clutch buttons, arm clutch and elevation clutch. DICOM Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) is a standard for storing and transmitting medical images enabling the integration of medical imaging devices such as scanners, servers, workstations, printers, network hardware, and picture archiving and communication systems (PACS) from multiple manufacturers. Dock Attach the Swivel Connector to the docking spar on the System Cart arm. Also referred to as docking. Docking spar The part of the arm that attaches to the Swivel Connector for docking. ET tube Endotracheal tube. ECG Electrocardiogram. ERD Endoscope Reprocessing Department. Fault, faulting The system generates a fault when it detects an anomaly. Fiducial Marker An object placed in or around the target that can be viewed with imaging tools. Fluoro Fluoroscopy. Fluoroscope An instrument with a fluorescent screen used for viewing x-ray images. Also referred to as C-arm. Instrument Tool used in the patient once attached to the arm. Instrument Arm See Arm. Leak Test A test used in reprocessing to determine if leaks are present in the Fully Articulating Catheter and Peripheral Vision Probe. Leak Test Port Used for leak testing. LED Light emitting diode. NA Not Applicable. Note User information to emphasize an important point. PACS Picture Archiving and Communication Systems (PACS) is a medical imaging technology which provides economical storage and convenient access to images from multiple modalities (source machine types). (continues on next page)

Also called Central Sterile Supply Department (CSSD) is a department in hospitals and other healthcare facilities that performs cleaning, sterilization and other actions on medical devices and equipment. Target The lesion, nodule, or tumor to be accessed for biopsy. Touchscreen The touchscreen monitor on the Controller. 349b327334995bee.text: The Ion System Cart (referred to as the System Cart) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract. The Ion Controller (referred to as the Controller) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract. The Ion Fully Articulating Catheter (referred to as the Catheter) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system for navigating to the target region in the airways. It is intended to also provide a conduit for the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe, Flexision Biopsy Needles and delivering compatible off-the-shelf tools. The Flexision Biopsy Needle is intended to retrieve tissue from a target structure. The Ion Peripheral Vision Probe (referred to as the Vision Probe) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system to provide live airway view for catheter navigation. The Vision Probe Adapter is intended to be used to connect the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. The Vision Probe Bag is used for temporary storage of the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe during a procedure. The Catheter Guide is intended to be used with the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to provide support. The Sensor Connection Cleaner is used for cleaning the sensor connections on the carriage of the Ion System Cart and the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. The Swivel Connector is intended to be used to connect the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to an endotracheal tube. The Suction Adapter is intended to allow modulation of suction when suction tubing is connected to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. Intended Patient Population The Ion endoluminal system (Model IF 1000) is intended for adult patients suitable for bronchoscopy. Patient general health and medical history must be adequately assessed along with potential benefits and risks prior to performing procedures with the Ion endoluminal system. These include but are not limited to risks associated with pulmonary disease, severe pulmonary hypertension, cardiovascular disease, bleeding disorders, thromboembolic disorders, anticoagulation therapy, anatomical constraints, inability to oxygenate and patient suitability for general anesthesia.

f5c9dfc75a15d46d.text: Only physicians with adequate training and experience in bronchoscopic techniques and adequate healthcare facilities should perform procedures with the Ion endoluminal system. Training provided by Intuitive is limited to the use of the Ion endoluminal system and does not replace the necessary medical training and experience required to perform diagnostic and therapeutic bronchoscopy procedures. As with any bronchoscopic procedure under general anesthesia, serious complications may include bleeding, pneumothorax (collapsed lung), cardiac-related complications, respiratory failure, air embolism, or death. As with other medical procedures, there may be additional risks associated with the use of general anesthesia and/or endotracheal intubation which are not listed above; patients should consult a healthcare professional regarding these and other potential risks. The overall benefit of the Ion endoluminal system is to bronchoscopically access and biopsy pulmonary lesions, including nodules in the lung periphery. The potential clinical benefits include improved or similar diagnostic outcomes of the sample obtained with comparable or fewer complications to other non-surgical approaches. The clinical benefits depend on a number of factors, including but not limited to nodule characteristics, patient medical history and disease state, and physician experience.

Intuitive Ion Endoluminal System

The Ion System Cart (referred to as the System Cart) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract. The Ion Controller (referred to as the Controller) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract. The Ion Fully Articulating Catheter (referred to as the Catheter) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system for navigating to the target region in the airways. It is intended to also provide a conduit for the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe, Flexision Biopsy Needles and delivering compatible off-the-shelf tools. The Flexision Biopsy Needle is intended to retrieve tissue from a target structure. The Ion Peripheral Vision Probe (referred to as the Vision Probe) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system to provide live airway view for catheter navigation. The Vision Probe Adapter is intended to be used to connect the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. The Vision Probe Bag is used for temporary storage of the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe during a procedure. The Catheter Guide is intended to be used with the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to provide support. The Sensor Connection Cleaner is used for cleaning the sensor connections on the carriage of the Ion System Cart and the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. The Swivel Connector is intended to be used to connect the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to an endotracheal tube. The Suction Adapter is intended to allow modulation of suction when suction tubing is connected to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. Intended Patient Population The Ion endoluminal system (Model IF 1000) is intended for adult patients suitable for bronchoscopy. Patient general health and medical history must be adequately assessed along with potential benefits and risks prior to performing procedures with the Ion endoluminal system. These include but are not limited to risks associated with pulmonary disease, severe pulmonary hypertension, cardiovascular disease, bleeding disorders, thromboembolic disorders, anticoagulation therapy, anatomical constraints, inability to oxygenate and patient suitability for general anesthesia.

Only physicians with adequate training and experience in bronchoscopic techniques and adequate healthcare facilities should perform procedures with the Ion endoluminal system. Training provided by Intuitive is limited to the use of the Ion endoluminal system and does not replace the necessary medical training and experience required to perform diagnostic and therapeutic bronchoscopy procedures. 4 Professional Instructions for Use

Patients should talk to their physician to decide if the Ion endoluminal system is right for them. As with any bronchoscopic procedure under general anesthesia, serious complications may include bleeding, pneumothorax (collapsed lung), cardiac-related complications, respiratory failure, air embolism, or death. As with other medical procedures, there may be additional risks associated with the use of general anesthesia and/or endotracheal intubation which are not listed above; patients should consult a healthcare professional regarding these and other potential risks. The overall benefit of the Ion endoluminal system is to bronchoscopically access and biopsy pulmonary lesions, including nodules in the lung periphery. The potential clinical benefits include improved or similar diagnostic outcomes of the sample obtained with comparable or fewer complications to other non-surgical approaches. The clinical benefits depend on a number of factors, including but not limited to nodule characteristics, patient medical history and disease state, and physician experience.

5 Serious Incident Reporting

Serious incident means any incident that directly or indirectly led, might have led, or might lead to any of the following: the death of a patient, user, or other person, • the temporary or permanent serious deterioration of a patient's, user's, or other person's • state of health, a serious public health threat. • For a patient/user/third party in the European Union and in countries with identical regulatory regime (Regulation /EU on Medical Devices); if, during the use of this device or as a result of its use, a serious incident has occurred, report the incident to the manufacturer and its authorized representative and to your national authority. 1. 6 General Warnings, Cautions, and Notes

Warnings

Before using the Ion endoluminal system (the system), review and understand

the content in this manual and all accompanying manuals and supplements.

To prevent patient harm, use only instruments, accessories, and third-party

products that are approved by Intuitive. Non-approved devices are not guaranteed to be compatible with the system.

Confirm that the sterile packaging for all single-use devices is intact and sealed

before use. Do not use contaminated single-use devices or reuse single-use devices, as this may result in patient infection or equipment damage.

To avoid risk of electric shock or equipment damage, do not step on, crush/

pinch, crimp, or otherwise stress cables and connectors.

Do not reuse or reprocess single-use devices (such as the Swivel Connector and

Vision Probe Adapter) after being removed from package, even if unused, as this may result in patient infection or device damage.

To prevent impaired ventilation and patient injury, the procedure should be

performed under general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation, Electrocardiography (ECG) monitoring, and ventilator alarms.

If the system, instruments and accessories, or any of their components cannot

be manipulated in a precise and controlled manner, discontinue use and contact Intuitive to prevent patient harm.

To prevent patient injury, do not use excessive force during the insertion or

extraction of the Vision Probe or bronchoscopic tools through the Catheter tool channel.

Use fluoroscopic visualization (fluoroscopy) when advancing tools past the tip

of the Catheter. Failure to use fluoroscopy during biopsy may result in patient injury.

Advance the Catheter only under live visualization from the Vision Probe

(Live View) to prevent procedural delay or patient injury.

Do not activate the scroll wheel while interacting with the Controller

touchscreen, as this may result in pneumothorax.

In the event of a medical emergency, follow steps to obtain immediate access

to the patient (emergency egress), to avoid delays in patient care.

Do not contaminate instruments or accessories before or during use, as

contamination may result in patient infection.

Handle biopsy needles with care to prevent user injury.

Always inspect the biopsy needle for damage before and during use. A damaged

needle can contain loose fragments that may cause toxic reaction if left in the patient.

Use caution during biopsy of targets within 5 mm of the visceral pleura or other

critical structures. Biopsy near critical structures may result in patient injury.

Insert the Vision Probe after biopsy to assess airways for trauma or bleeding to

prevent delayed intervention in case of an emergency.

Follow proper system and Controller cleaning procedures to prevent patient

infection.

Cautions

The system may be unpacked, installed, and serviced by Intuitive personnel only.

Do not attempt to unpack, install, or service equipment without Intuitive personnel, as this may result in user harm.

No modification of this equipment is allowed. Failure to comply may result in

user or patient harm.

To avoid the risk of electric shock, this equipment must only be connected to a

supply mains with protective earth.

Note that conversion to alternate technique during the procedure may prolong

anesthesia time.

Leakage current from interconnected medical equipment (for example,

ultrasound equipment) may exceed safe levels. To maintain the safety of patients and users, interconnect only with devices that comply with IEC 60601-1, and whose total patient leakage current meets the limits of Clause 16 of IEC 60601-1 (third edition or higher).

Leakage current from interconnected electrical equipment (for example,

external displays) may exceed safe levels. To maintain the safety of patients and users, interconnect only with devices in compliance with IEC 60601-1-1. Users must ensure that any interconnected equipment not supplied by Intuitive maintains compliance with IEC 60601-1-1.

Do not cover any ventilation openings on the system or on the arm. Covering

ventilation openings may cause improper function of the system.

Inspect all instruments and accessories for potential damage prior to clinical use

to prevent procedure delay.

Exercise caution when inserting the biopsy needle into the Catheter tool channel

with the sheath extended. Failure to do so may result in patient injury.

To prevent impaired lung function, limit the total volume of saline injection for

Vision Probe cleaning to less than 40 m L.

If resistance is felt when removing the Vision Probe or tool from the Catheter tool

channel, do not continue retracting the device, as this may result in device damage. Remove the Catheter and Vision Probe or tool together.

The Ion System Cart (referred to as the System Cart) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract. The Ion Controller (referred to as the Controller) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract. The Ion Fully Articulating Catheter (referred to as the Catheter) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system for navigating to the target region in the airways. It is intended to also provide a conduit for the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe, Flexision Biopsy Needles and delivering compatible off-the-shelf tools. The Flexision Biopsy Needle is intended to retrieve tissue from a target structure. The Ion Peripheral Vision Probe (referred to as the Vision Probe) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system to provide live airway view for catheter navigation. The Vision Probe Adapter is intended to be used to connect the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. The Vision Probe Bag is used for temporary storage of the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe during a procedure. The Catheter Guide is intended to be used with the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to provide support. The Sensor Connection Cleaner is used for cleaning the sensor connections on the carriage of the Ion System Cart and the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. The Swivel Connector is intended to be used to connect the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to an endotracheal tube. The Suction Adapter is intended to allow modulation of suction when suction tubing is connected to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. Intended Patient Population The Ion endoluminal system (Model IF 1000) is intended for adult patients suitable for bronchoscopy. Patient general health and medical history must be adequately assessed along with potential benefits and risks prior to performing procedures with the Ion endoluminal system. These include but are not limited to risks associated with pulmonary disease, severe pulmonary hypertension, cardiovascular disease, bleeding disorders, thromboembolic disorders, anticoagulation therapy, anatomical constraints, inability to oxygenate and patient suitability for general anesthesia.

1. 4 Professional Instructions for Use Essential Prescribing Information Device Name: Intuitive Ion Endoluminal System and Instruments (IF 1000). • Rx only: Federal Law (USA) restricts this device to sale by or on the order of a physician (or • properly licensed practitioner). Indications for Use The Ion endoluminal system (Model IF 1000), referred to in this manual as “the system, ” assists the user in navigating a catheter and endoscopic tools in the pulmonary tract using endoscopic visualization of the tracheobronchial tree for diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. The Ion endoluminal system enables fiducial marker placement. It does not make a diagnosis and is not for pediatric use. The Plan Point Software uses patient CT scans to create a 3 D plan of the lung and navigation pathways for use with the Ion endoluminal system. The Flexision Biopsy Needle is used with the Ion endoluminal system to biopsy tissue from a target area in the lung.

12 Introduction | Professional Instructions for Use Intended Use The Ion System Cart (referred to as the System Cart) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract. The Ion Controller (referred to as the Controller) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract. The Ion Fully Articulating Catheter (referred to as the Catheter) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system for navigating to the target region in the airways. It is intended to also provide a conduit for the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe, Flexision Biopsy Needles and delivering compatible off-the-shelf tools. The Flexision Biopsy Needle is intended to retrieve tissue from a target structure. The Ion Peripheral Vision Probe (referred to as the Vision Probe) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system to provide live airway view for catheter navigation. The Vision Probe Adapter is intended to be used to connect the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. The Vision Probe Bag is used for temporary storage of the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe during a procedure. The Catheter Guide is intended to be used with the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to provide support. The Sensor Connection Cleaner is used for cleaning the sensor connections on the carriage of the Ion System Cart and the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. The Swivel Connector is intended to be used to connect the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to an endotracheal tube. The Suction Adapter is intended to allow modulation of suction when suction tubing is connected to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. Intended Patient Population The Ion endoluminal system (Model IF

1000) is intended for adult patients suitable for bronchoscopy. Patient general health and medical history must be adequately assessed along with potential benefits and risks prior to performing procedures with the Ion endoluminal system. These include but are not limited to risks associated with pulmonary disease, severe pulmonary hypertension, cardiovascular disease, bleeding disorders, thromboembolic disorders, anticoagulation therapy, anatomical constraints, inability to oxygenate and patient suitability for general anesthesia. Intended User Only physicians with adequate training and experience in bronchoscopic techniques and adequate healthcare facilities should perform procedures with the Ion endoluminal system. Training provided by Intuitive is limited to the use of the Ion endoluminal system and does not replace the necessary medical training and experience required to perform diagnostic and therapeutic bronchoscopy procedures.

Introduction | Serious Incident Reporting 13 Clinical Risks and Benefits Patients should talk to their physician to decide if the Ion endoluminal system is right for them. As with any bronchoscopic procedure under general anesthesia, serious complications may include bleeding, pneumothorax (collapsed lung), cardiac-related complications, respiratory failure, air embolism, or death. As with other medical procedures, there may be additional risks associated with the use of general anesthesia and/or endotracheal intubation which are not listed above; patients should consult a healthcare professional regarding these and other potential risks. The overall benefit of the Ion endoluminal system is to bronchoscopically access and biopsy pulmonary lesions, including nodules in the lung periphery. The potential clinical benefits include improved or similar diagnostic outcomes of the sample obtained with comparable or fewer complications to other non-surgical approaches. The clinical benefits depend on a number of factors, including but not limited to nodule characteristics, patient medical history and disease state, and physician experience.

1. 6 General Warnings, Cautions, and Notes Warnings WARNING: Before using the Ion endoluminal system (the system), review and understand the content in this manual and all accompanying manuals and supplements. WARNING: To prevent patient harm, use only instruments, accessories, and third-party products that are approved by Intuitive. Non-approved devices are not guaranteed to be compatible with the system. WARNING: Confirm that the sterile packaging for all single-use devices is intact and sealed before use. Do not use contaminated single-use devices or reuse single-use devices, as this may result in patient infection or equipment damage. WARNING: To avoid risk of electric shock or equipment damage, do not step on, crush/ pinch, crimp, or otherwise stress cables and connectors. WARNING: Do not reuse or reprocess single-use devices (such as the Swivel Connector and Vision Probe Adapter) after being removed from package, even if unused, as this may result in patient infection or device damage. WARNING: To prevent impaired ventilation and patient injury, the procedure should be performed under general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation, Electrocardiography (ECG) monitoring, and ventilator alarms. WARNING: If the system, instruments and accessories, or any of their components cannot be manipulated in a precise and controlled manner, discontinue use and contact Intuitive to prevent patient harm. WARNING: To prevent patient injury, do not use excessive force during the insertion or extraction of the Vision Probe or bronchoscopic tools through the Catheter tool channel. WARNING: Use fluoroscopic visualization (fluoroscopy) when advancing tools past the tip of the Catheter. Failure to use fluoroscopy during biopsy may result in patient injury. WARNING: Advance the Catheter only under live visualization from the Vision Probe (Live View) to prevent procedural delay or patient injury. WARNING: Do not activate the scroll wheel while interacting with the Controller touchscreen, as this may result in pneumothorax. WARNING: In the event of a medical emergency, follow steps to obtain immediate access to the patient (emergency egress), to avoid delays in patient care. WARNING: Do not contaminate instruments or accessories before or during use, as contamination may result in patient infection. WARNING: Handle biopsy needles with care to prevent user injury. WARNING: Always inspect the biopsy needle for damage before and during use. A damaged needle can contain loose fragments that may cause toxic reaction if left in the patient. WARNING: Use caution during biopsy of targets within 5 mm of the visceral pleura or other critical structures. Biopsy near critical structures may result in patient injury.

32 System Overview | Device Description The Flexision Biopsy Needles (referred to as biopsy needles, or needles) are flexible needles compatible with the Catheter. Biopsy needles come in 19 G, 21 G, and 23 G sizes and are protected by a flexible retractable sheath, with a stylet for support during insertion. The needle and sheath tip are radiopaque for visualization under fluoroscopy. The needle handle contains a catch (detent) that creates resistance to hold the handle in place until the user pushes the handle past the catch (detent). The needle stop allows the user to control the needle length (up to 3 cm). The biopsy needles are packaged with a compatible three-way valve and vacuum syringe. The biopsy needles are single-use devices provided sterile by Ethylene Oxide (EO) sterilization method. For replacement, contact Customer Service.

4. 3 Controller Use The Controller provides controls to insert, retract, and articulate the Catheter. Note: If friction is felt in the trackball or scroll wheel, clean it with saline and dry with gauze prior to or during use, as needed. Note: Calibration initiates after installing the trackball and scroll wheel. Do not touch the trackball or scroll wheel during calibration. Note: If Controller responsiveness is poor, change or dry gloves. The Controller touchscreen and scroll wheel are designed to sense touch. Wet gloves may interfere with touch sensing. Figure

4. 19 Controller 4 3 5 6 2 1 7 8 10 9 The Controller has the following components:

1. Handle: Provides grasp for transport of the Controller.

2. Emergency stop (E-stop) button: Stops system operation at any time and causes the Catheter tip to go inactive.

3. Scroll wheel: Controls the insertion and retraction of the Catheter. Roll it towards the touchscreen to insert the Catheter, and roll it away from the touchscreen to retract it.

4. Passive button: Controls the Catheter state (active and passive). Quick-press this button to relax the Catheter tip (passive), and press it again to resume active mode. Press and hold to slowly relax the Catheter tip (temporary passive). Release the button to stop relaxing the Catheter and resume active mode.

5. Touchscreen: Controls to select targets, save images and videos, and provide other options described in this manual.

6. Trackball: Controls the articulation of the Catheter tip. Roll the trackball right to move the Catheter tip to the right, roll the trackball left to move the Catheter tip to the left. Roll up and down to move the Catheter tip up and down.

7. USB inputs: Connects the USB storage device to the Controller. There are two options: USB-A and USB-C. Either input can be used, depending on the connector type.

8. Magnet: A magnet attached to the Controller that can be used to remove the trackball.

9. 1 Register WARNING: To prevent impaired ventilation and patient injury, the procedure should be performed under general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation, Electrocardiography (ECG) monitoring, and ventilator alarms. Registration is the process used to match the airway Live View with the Navigation View. During registration, the system collects apical and basal data for each lung. These apical and basal segments are displayed on the system as four quadrants, which are regional divisions of the Airway Tree (that is, the quadrants are not anatomically divided by lobe). Follow the steps on the top monitor to perform airway registration.

1. Drive to main carina. a. Match the Live View to the Navigation View in centering, depth, and rotation. If the views do not match, adjust the Live View as needed. Adjust centering using the trackball, adjust depth using the scroll wheel, or adjust rotation using the Controller touchscreen. b. Tap Confirm Main Carina on the Controller touchscreen.

2. If you would like to start video recording, tap Start Video. This button is always accessible from the Quick Tools panel.

3. Start survey by driving into each main bronchus until the right and left indicators are illuminated.
76 Procedure and Biopsy | Register

4. Drive into one apical and one basal segment in each lung until the indicator for each quadrant illuminates. The border of the quadrant you are currently in is highlighted. Note: Use Show Lung Regions to display the separation of the lung into the four quadrants with their associated colors on the Airway Tree (note that these quadrants are not based on lobes). If the system checks the wrong quadrant, continue to drive to all four apical and basal regions of the lung. If quadrant checks are missing after you have navigated to all four regions, proceed with partial registration. It is not recommended to continue navigating to get all four quadrant checks if apical and basal data has been gathered. Figure

9. 1 Register anatomy (example)

5. Evaluate registration and tap Accept Registration or Redo Registration on the Controller touchscreen. To evaluate registration, navigate beyond the main carina and evaluate the relationship between the Live View and the Navigation View, especially at carinas proximal to the region of interest. Some discrepancy may occur due to biological motion. Redo registration if there is a visual mismatch between the Live View and Navigation View • during navigation, or if there is significant patient or system movement. Redo registration if the Swivel Connector is undocked from the arm, the arm clutch button is • pressed, the System Cart brakes are unlocked, or the Catheter is removed from the system mid-procedure.

9. 2 Navigate After registration is complete, the first planned destination (target and path) automatically appears on screen. The planned pathway to the target appears on the Navigation View, Tree View, and Progress View. It is possible to switch to an alternate target or pathway if one was planned. Navigation of the Catheter through the airways should be performed in a minimally traumatic manner by attempting to stay in the center of the airways at all times. WARNING: Advance the Catheter only under live visualization from the Vision Probe (Live View) to prevent procedural delay or patient injury. WARNING: Do not activate the scroll wheel while interacting with the Controller touchscreen, as this may result in pneumothorax. Note: Navigation View should be used as guidance only. Note: The Swivel Connector may partially disconnect from the arm due to Catheter buckling or excessive friction in the ET tube. Ensure sufficient lubrication is applied to the Catheter. To navigate to the target and position the Catheter for biopsy:

1. Use the Controller to drive the Catheter through the planned pathway to the target. Watch the Live View while driving.

2. Once the target is reached, note the message to use fluoroscopic guidance when extending tools past the tip of the Catheter.

3. (Optional) Perform a radial endobronchial ultrasound (R-EBUS) using fluoroscopy to confirm the target location. a. Position the Catheter for R-EBUS approximately 10 mm proximal to the lesion. Ensure there is a small gap between the tip of the Catheter and the airway wall to allow the R-EBUS probe to exit the Catheter. If needed, pull back the Vision Probe slightly to visually confirm that the Catheter points to the airway wall. b. Adjust the fluoroscope to match the optimal fluoro angle on the top monitor. c. Remove the Vision Probe from the Catheter and keep the Vision Probe out of the way by placing it into the Vision Probe Bag. d. Perform R-EBUS. If needed, use Fluoro Reference and Articulation Guide with R-EBUS to localize the target (see Biopsy Tab on page 41). e. If needed, select Move Target to update the target position (see Biopsy Tab on page 41). f. Re-insert the Vision Probe into the Catheter.
78 Procedure and Biopsy | Biopsy Overview

4. Position the Catheter for biopsy. Using Navigation View for reference, aim the Catheter as straight as possible toward the • center of the target. Ensure the target is within striking distance of the needle (approximately 30 mm). • For endoluminal targets: Position the Catheter tip directly against the target. • For extra bronchial targets: Position the Catheter tip against the airway wall for stability. If • needed, pull the Vision Probe back slightly to visually confirm that the Catheter tip sits directly against the airway wall.

5. Remove the Vision Probe from the Catheter and keep the Vision Probe out of the way by placing it into the Vision Probe bag.

6. For biopsy, adjust the fluoroscope to match the optimal fluoro angle on the top monitor.

9. 4 Flexision Needle Biopsy WARNING: Always inspect the biopsy needle for damage before and during use. A damaged needle can contain loose fragments that may cause toxic reaction if left in the patient. WARNING: Use fluoroscopic visualization (fluoroscopy) when advancing tools past the tip of the Catheter. Failure to use fluoroscopy during biopsy may result in patient injury. WARNING: Always reset the needle stop (re-sheath the needle): before removing the biopsy needle from the Catheter tool channel, after preparing the sample, or before transferring the needle between staff. Failure to reset the needle stop during handling or hand-offs may result in infection or injury by needle stick. WARNING: If you notice damage to the inside of the Catheter during use, replace the Catheter. A damaged Catheter can contain loose fragments that may cause toxic reaction if left in the patient. CAUTION: Proceed with caution if the biopsy needle is inserted or removed through a Catheter bend radius smaller than 15 mm. Insertion and removal of the biopsy needle should not be performed against increased resistance. Failure to follow instructions may result in Catheter or needle damage. CAUTION: Exercise caution when inserting the biopsy needle into the Catheter tool channel with the sheath extended. Failure to do so may result in patient injury.

1. Inspect the biopsy needle prior to use. If damaged, dispose and replace the needle. a. Before use of the needle, confirm the label is legible and is the intended needle size. b. Before use and between each use, inspect the needle for the following: Damage to sheath shaft, sheath tip, needle tube, and needle point (for example, burrs or • dull edges at needle point, loose or separated needle, or kinks). Foreign matter. • Friction when extending needle, or inability to fully extend needle (approximately 3 cm). • Blocked or kinked lumen. Check by flushing with saline. • Ensure needle stop is functioning properly. Proper function is described as: When the needle stop is pressed, the needle stop should slide freely. • When the needle stop is released, the needle stop should be locked. • Stylet does not extend beyond the tip of the needle (more than 3 mm). • c. Before inserting or reinserting into the Catheter tool channel, confirm the needle is fully retracted and locked within the sheath, the needle sheath home position mark is fully exposed, and the thumbscrew has locked the sheath extension.

2. Insert the biopsy needle through the Catheter tool channel. Secure the needle to the Catheter.
Procedure and Biopsy | Flexision Needle Biopsy 81

3. Under fluoroscopy, position the sheath for biopsy. Position the sheath so that it extends slightly beyond the Catheter, by loosening the thumbscrew on the needle handle. Approximately 1⁄4 (one-fourth) turn of the thumbscrew allows the sheath to move back and forth. a. Look for tenting under fluoroscopy (indicated by backward movement of the Catheter). b. Confirm that the Catheter and sheath are aligned to the target. c. After placement of the sheath tip, tighten the thumbscrew to lock the sheath position. WARNING: Confirm the relation of the patient anatomy to the biopsy target (for example, distances to target and anatomy borders) before setting needle stroke length. Setting the incorrect needle stroke length may lead to pneumothorax.

4. While stabilizing the needle handle, set the needle insertion depth using the needle stop up to 3 cm based on the distance to the target and size of the target. The insertion distance should be based on physician discretion. The estimated distance of the Catheter to the target is shown on the monitor. Consider minimum distance to target as provided by the navigation, sheath extension, and fluoroscopy before choosing a needle extension length.

5. Under fluoroscopy, insert the needle with one jab towards the target. If needed, check the recommended fluoro arm angle on the monitor and adjust the fluoro arm.

6. Once the needle is inserted, remove the stylet from the back end of the needle while holding the needle in place. At the physician’s discretion, suction can be attached to the needle. For suction, connect the stopcock to the vacuum syringe provided with the needle. With the stopcock closed, pull back vacuum for 5 to 20 m L. Connect the stopcock to the needle and open the valve towards the needle. Note: Select a vacuum locking syringe and stopcock with standard luer lock connectors (luer fittings compliant with ISO 80369-7) that can suction up to 20 m L.

7. Perform multiple jabs with the needle, per physician discretion.

8. Remove the vacuum syringe and, under fluoroscopy, fully retract the needle into the sheath, and return the needle stop to the home position.

9. If desired, fully retract the sheath and tighten the thumbscrew. If you opt to keep the sheath extended for further passes, exercise caution when re-inserting the needle into the Catheter tool channel.

10. Press the connector key and pull the biopsy needle from the Catheter tool channel.
11. Evaluate airway. Perform airway evaluation after all the biopsy passes are complete. Insert the Vision Probe into the Catheter to evaluate the biopsy site for any bleeding.

6. Once adjustments are made, re-dock the system, insert the lubricated Catheter back into the ET tube, extend the Catheter Guide, and advance the Catheter.

7. Perform registration again. A. 5 Unable to Complete Registration If the survey for one or both of the main bronchi cannot be completed, tap Proceed with Partial Survey on the Controller touchscreen to accept the partial survey and continue to the next step of registration. If the survey for one or more of the regions cannot be completed, use the Show Lung Regions feature to assist in identifying airways in that region. Then, tap Proceed with Partial Registration on the Controller touchscreen to accept the partial registration and continue to the final step of registration. Note: You will need to register 4 cm on each side of the main carina to complete registration.

96 Troubleshooting | Registration with Variant Anatomy A. 6 Registration with Variant Anatomy If the patient has had a previous resection, use Show Lung Regions to view the corresponding quadrant assignments on the top monitor. Use these quadrant assignments as a guide during registration. If the main carina point is not situated at the anatomical main carina (for example, due to a pneumonectomy), still navigate to this main carina point and begin registration from there. Again, use Show Lung Regions to assist with registration. If you are unable to complete the quadrant survey, ensure that apical and basal regions of the lung are registered and proceed with partial registration. If needed, you can review the plan on the Planning Laptop to perform further troubleshooting. See the troubleshooting information in the Plan Point Softwareand Planning Laptop Supplement. A. 7 Inaccurate Registration (Navigation and Live View Mismatch) If the Navigation View does not match the Live View and does not allow you to navigate accurately, redo registration. On the Controller touchscreen, select the Register tab and tap Redo Registration. Confirm your choice on the touchscreen and follow the steps to complete registration again. Consider performing registration under a patient breath hold. Assess registration accuracy using the Live View, Navigation View, and Tree View. If the mismatch between the Navigation View and Live View is consistent, especially due to rotational or depth offsets in the periphery of the lungs, use Lock to Path mode to adjust the Navigation View to match the Live View, and then update the target location using Move Target. See and Biopsy Tab on page 41 for more information on the Lock to Path and Move Target functionality. A. 8 USB Errors Error Reading USB The system cannot read the USB. Try re-inserting the USB. If the issue persists, use a different USB drive. Note: If a plan has already been loaded when you get this error, you may continue with the loaded plan, but note that you cannot take screenshots, record video, or load new plans unless you restart the system. USB Not Valid The system does not recognize the USB. Confirm that a compatible and formatted USB is used. The USB file system should be either FAT/FAT 32 or NTFS. If the issue persists after confirming your USB's compatibility and formatting, use a different USB drive.

Troubleshooting | Catheter Not Moving (Controls Unresponsive) 99 A. 11 Catheter Not Moving (Controls Unresponsive) If the Catheter is not moving or the trackball or scroll wheel is not responding, ensure that the Catheter Guide and Swivel Connector are securely connected to the docking spar. If the Catheter Guide and Swivel Connector are connected to the docking spar, remove the trackball or scroll wheel from its cup, reinstall, and wait for calibration. Clean the trackball or scroll wheel if necessary, and ensure that both are reinstalled fully into their cups. If the issue persists, try any of the following: Clean the Catheter Guide connections. • Restart the system. • Install a new Catheter Guide. • A. 12 Rotated Vision Probe View (Non-intuitive Driving) When inserting the Vision Probe through the Catheter, the system will detect the color stripes inside the Catheter to ensure vision is oriented correctly while driving. If the stripes are not visible, a message appears when the Vision Probe reaches the Catheter tip. The message indicates that orientation was not accurately detected and instructs you to partially retract the Vision Probe until the stripes inside the Catheter are clearly visible, and then reinsert the Vision Probe through the Catheter. Always make sure the Vision Probe tip is clean. If the system does not present the message because it did not detect the stripes (or if it detects the stripes incorrectly), the Vision Probe image will appear to be 90 or 180 degrees rotated, and driving will be non-intuitive. In this case, partially retract the Vision Probe until the stripes inside the Catheter are clearly visible, and then reinsert the Vision Probe through the Catheter. If the issue persists, try replacing the Vision Probe, the Catheter, or both. A. 13 Live View Displays Colored Lines If the Live View (Vision Probe view) on the bottom monitor displays colored lines, install a new Vision Probe onto the system and ensure that the leak test port remains closed. Check the leak test port of the old Vision Probe for fluid or condensation. If no fluid is present, the Vision Probe may have been damaged due to a tight turn or bend radius.

Otherwise, remove the Vision Probe from the Catheter, wipe the Vision Probe tip, and re-insert the Vision Probe. If there are secretions within the Catheter tool channel, •

1. Retract the Catheter Guide and remove the Catheter from the ET tube.

2. Remove the Vision Probe from the Catheter.

Elevated drive force may indicate that the Swivel • Connector is susceptible to disconnecting from the arm. A. 18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference) If the top monitor displays a grey spinning wheel during navigation, there is an interruption in the Catheter sensor connection due to a tight bend radius (tight turn in the Catheter tip). To resolve the issue:

1. If needed, mark the original Catheter position with a biopsy marker.

2. Straighten the Catheter using any of the following methods: Articulate the trackball in the direction of the white arrow that is displayed on the tip • indicator. Press the Passive button on the Controller. • Slightly retract the Catheter. • If the issue persists, the following may improve tight turn navigation: Re-lubricate the Catheter. • Undock and retract the ET tube (which requires re-registering). This gives the Catheter more • length beyond the tip of the ET tube, which allows the Catheter to build more support against the trachea wall to make a wider turn. Under fluoroscopy, monitor the Catheter and look for a delay in Catheter advancement as indication that you are building support against the trachea wall. Use the carriage clutch button to retract the carriage and release tension. • A. 19 Touchscreen Unresponsive If the Controller touchscreen is unresponsive, the system may detect fluid on the screen. Wipe any visible fluid from the screen and wait five seconds before attempting to make a selection. Otherwise, wait five seconds before making a selection. If the issue persists, restart the system.

To recover the monitor feed, troubleshoot as follows: Note: After performing the troubleshooting steps below, if only one monitor returns to a live feed, perform a mid-procedure restart to resolve the issue. If the monitors time out during the procedure and the monitor timeout notification appears, • select Recover on the Controller touchscreen to resolve the issue. If the monitors time out when you plug in or unplug an external display or recording device • from the System Cart, select Continue on the Controller touchscreen to synchronize the monitors, and then select Recover to resolve the issue. A. 21 System Faults When a system fault occurs, the system displays a message on the monitor, the instrument arm locks, and the Catheter becomes inactive. WARNING: When a system fault occurs, retract the tool inside the protective sheath immediately to minimize interaction with tissue and prevent patient injury as the Catheter slowly relaxes in response to the fault. CAUTION: Failure to recognize and recover from system faults may result in procedure delay. Non-Recoverable Fault In the event of a non-recoverable fault, system LED s illuminate red (if applicable). See A. 2 Midprocedure Restart on page

94. If the fault persists, contact Customer Service to troubleshoot the issue. Recoverable Fault In the event of a recoverable fault, system LED s illuminate yellow on the part of the system that needs attention to recover the fault (if applicable). Follow system messages to recover and continue with the procedure. Or, tap Recover Fault on the Controller touchscreen. A. 22 Patient Motion The system detects if there is significant patient motion, and shows a notification on the top monitor. If patient motion is detected, evaluate registration accuracy by ensuring the Live View matches with the Navigation View while driving. Perform one of the following steps: If registration is accurate, tap Dismiss. • If registration is not accurate, tap Redo Registration to perform registration again. • Note: Catheter buckling or excessive friction in the ET tube may be detected as patient motion, and result in a patient motion notification from the system. Ensure sufficient lubrication is applied to the Catheter.

122 Glossary Appendix G Glossary Table G. 1 Glossary Meaning Term 3 D Three-dimensional. AC Alternating current, also represented by the AC symbol: ~. “AC” or “AC power” refers to electrical connection to a wall outlet, as opposed to battery power. AP View Anterior-posterior view. Head on view of the airway tree looking straight at the patient’s chest. Arm The instrument arm on the System Cart that supports the Catheter, Catheter Guide, Vision Probe, and accessories. BF or Type BF An IEC 60601-1 classification for patient applied parts. A Type BF classification indicates an applied part that is not suitable for direct conductive contact with the heart or other applications as considered necessary. Bronchoscopy An endoscopic technique of visualizing the inside of the airways for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes where a bronchoscope is introduced through nose or mouth. It is a non-sterile procedure. Bronch Suite See Procedure Room. C-arm See fluoroscope. CF or Type CF An IEC 60601-1 classification for patient applied parts. Type CF is the most stringent classification, being required for those applications where the applied part is in direct conductive contact with the heart or other applications as considered necessary. CAUTION A caution alerts the reader about a potentially hazardous situation which, if not avoided, may result in minor or moderate injury to the user or patient or damage to the equipment or other property. It may also be used to alert against unsafe practices. This includes the special care necessary for the safe and effective use of the device and the care necessary to avoid damage to a device that may occur as a result of use or misuse. CSSD See SPD. Carriage The mechanism on the arm that supports the Catheter. Provides the insertion and retraction motion of the Catheter. Circulating nurse A circulating nurse is a non-sterile user. (continues on next page)

Glossary 123 Table G. 1 Glossary (continued) Meaning Term Clutch button Used to position the arm. There are two clutch buttons, arm clutch and elevation clutch. DICOM Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) is a standard for storing and transmitting medical images enabling the integration of medical imaging devices such as scanners, servers, workstations, printers, network hardware, and picture archiving and communication systems (PACS) from multiple manufacturers. Dock Attach the Swivel Connector to the docking spar on the System Cart arm. Also referred to as docking. Docking spar The part of the arm that attaches to the Swivel Connector for docking. ET tube Endotracheal tube. ECG Electrocardiogram. ERD Endoscope Reprocessing Department. Fault, faulting The system generates a fault when it detects an anomaly. Fiducial Marker An object placed in or around the target that can be viewed with imaging tools. Fluoro Fluoroscopy. Fluoroscope An instrument with a fluorescent screen used for viewing x-ray images. Also referred to as C-arm. Instrument Tool used in the patient once attached to the arm. Instrument Arm See Arm. Leak Test A test used in reprocessing to determine if leaks are present in the Fully Articulating Catheter and Peripheral Vision Probe. Leak Test Port Used for leak testing. LED Light emitting diode. NA Not Applicable. Note User information to emphasize an important point. PACS Picture Archiving and Communication Systems (PACS) is a medical imaging technology which provides economical storage and convenient access to images from multiple modalities (source machine types). Target The lesion, nodule, or tumor to be accessed for biopsy. Touchscreen The touchscreen monitor on the Controller. indications_for_use: The Ion System Cart (referred to as the System Cart) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract. The Ion Controller (referred to as the Controller) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract. The Ion Fully Articulating Catheter (referred to as the Catheter) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system for navigating to the target region in the airways. It is intended to also provide a conduit for the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe, Flexision Biopsy Needles and delivering compatible off-the-shelf tools. The Flexision Biopsy Needle is intended to retrieve tissue from a target structure. The Ion Peripheral Vision Probe (referred to as the Vision Probe) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system to provide live airway view for catheter navigation. The Vision Probe Adapter is intended to be used to connect the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. The Vision Probe Bag is used for temporary storage of the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe during a procedure. The Catheter Guide is intended to be used with the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to provide support. The Sensor Connection Cleaner is used for cleaning the sensor connections on the carriage of the Ion System Cart and the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. The Swivel Connector is intended to be used to connect the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to an endotracheal tube. The Suction Adapter is intended to allow modulation of suction when suction tubing is connected to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter. Intended Patient Population The Ion endoluminal system (Model IF 1000) is intended for adult patients suitable for bronchoscopy. Patient general health and medical history must be adequately assessed along with potential benefits and risks prior to performing procedures with the Ion endoluminal system. These include but are not limited to risks associated with pulmonary disease, severe pulmonary hypertension, cardiovascular disease, bleeding disorders, thromboembolic disorders, anticoagulation therapy, anatomical constraints, inability to oxygenate and patient suitability for general anesthesia.

safety_blocks.text: Patients should talk to their physician to decide if the Ion endoluminal system is right for them. As with any bronchoscopic procedure under general anesthesia, serious complications may include bleeding, pneumothorax (collapsed lung), cardiac-related complications, respiratory failure, air embolism, or death. As with other medical procedures, there may be additional risks associated with the use of general anesthesia and/or endotracheal intubation which are not listed above; patients should consult a healthcare professional regarding these and other potential risks. The overall benefit of the Ion endoluminal system is to bronchoscopically access and biopsy pulmonary lesions, including nodules in the lung periphery. The potential clinical benefits include improved or similar diagnostic outcomes of the sample obtained with comparable or fewer complications to other non-surgical approaches. The clinical benefits depend on a number of factors, including but not limited to nodule characteristics, patient medical history and disease state, and physician experience.
